safety: Back up your data before any repair step.
A swollen, hot, hissing or leaking battery: stop, power off, don't charge it, keep it away from anything flammable, and take it to a repair shop or battery recycler.
Opening a device can void its warranty. If it's under warranty or AppleCare/protection plan, contact the maker first.
Unplug the power and remove the battery where possible before opening anything.
Never open a power supply, charger or TV/console power unit: they hold dangerous charge even when unplugged.

symptoms.title: Not enough storage for games or updates

steps.do: Open the console's storage settings and sort games by size.
steps.why: Shows which games you can remove and reinstall later.

steps.do: Delete games you aren't playing; saves usually stay in the cloud or on the console.
Add the maker's supported external storage (USB drive, expansion card or microSD for Switch).
steps.why: Extends space without opening the console.

symptoms.title: Console is loud, hot or shuts off

steps.do: Give it 10-15 cm of space on every side and keep it out of cabinets.
Power off, unplug, and clean the outside vents with a soft brush or a vacuum on low.
steps.why: Dust on the vents blocks airflow.

steps.do: Stand it the way the maker recommends and keep it off carpet.
steps.why: Carpet and blocked vents trap heat.

stop_if: It shuts off on its own after cleaning
Opening it would be needed (this voids most console warranties)

symptoms.title: Controller won't connect, drifts or won't charge

steps.do: Charge it with a different cable, then re-pair it using the console's pairing steps.
steps.why: Pairing records and cables are the usual cause.

steps.do: Update the controller firmware from the console's settings.
steps.why: Updates fix many connection and drift problems.

steps.do: Use the console's stick calibration if it has one.
steps.why: Small drift can often be calibrated out.

stop_if: Drift remains after calibration and updates (stick wear: maker repair or replacement)

symptoms.title: Games crash or the console is slow

steps.do: Fully power off (not rest mode), unplug for 1 minute, and start again.

steps.why: Crashes are often fixed by patches.

steps.do: Use the console's built-in database rebuild or cache clear, if it has one (for example PlayStation Safe Mode).
steps.why: Fixes slow menus without deleting games.

stop_if: Errors that mention storage or hardware even after updates
